ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides who fixes, whether to resume or start fresh, and how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on `sonnet`. The change is small and has one clear answer, so the standard tier is enough. The brief names the Task 4 brief and the reviewer's report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`, and gives finding F1 as written. It asks the subagent to:
1. Write a failing test in `tests/test_retry.py` that pins the exact number of retries.
2. Change `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries` at `fetch/retry.py:41`.
3. Run the tests and commit.

ACTION: After the fix commit, generate a new diff file with `scripts/review-package` and dispatch a scoped re-review from `re-review-prompt.md`. It checks only F1 and any new Critical or Important issue. When it comes back clean, I append the Task 4 line to the ledger and start Task 5.

Message to my partner:

> The reviewer found one Important issue in Task 4. `fetch/retry.py:41` uses `>` where it needs `>=`, so the client retries one time more than configured.
>
> I am not fixing this myself, although you said to fix tiny things. My rule lets me make only edits that change no behavior, such as a typo in a doc. This edit is one character, but it changes how many times the code retries. So a fix subagent makes it. I have dispatched one now.
>
> The existing test only checks that a retry happens, not how many. That gap let the bug through. The subagent will first add a test that pins the exact retry count, so the fix has a test that covers it.
>
> `★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
> A test that asserts "a retry happens" passes for both `>` and `>=`. Only a test on the exact count tells the two apart.
> `─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
>
> A scoped re-review follows the fix. I continue to Task 5 when it is clean.
